| [CASE-355](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-355.md) | Registered evaluation in synthetic organizations | [LEAD-017](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-017.md) asked for A13's three organizations of matched behaviour and different endorsement relations, and a measure of registration that does not read the experimenter's setting ([QUESTION-270](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-270.md)'s second requirement). A consummatory process H evaluates it, and pursuit P keeps choosing it at a calibrated rate of 0.6 in all three organizations. In the denied organization H's evaluation is written into the organization's record and has no authority over pursuit. In the accommodating one it is written and has authority beyond a tolerance that reciprocal compensation widens. In the unregistered one it is never written. The record is mixed by an unknown rotation and noisy. The measure perturbs H's evaluation at random, as a hotspot probe would, and asks whether the record responds, holding fixed the outcome, the action and P's learned value. It was not fooled by a decoy record carrying the evaluation's physiological cause by another route (2% false calls, against 77% for the passive reading), nor by an evaluation that steers pursuit directly, bypassing the record (1.5%).
